title: Storage Fabric durability boundary
summary: dev6 integrates Storage Fabric v0.1-dev7 without creating a private ML storage authority. ML exports value-only checkpoint/frontier identity; Storage Fabric owns workspace placement, lifecycle, verification, replica safety and durable-completion truth.
authority: Storage Fabric dev7 is authoritative for storage semantics; ooRexx ML dev6 bridge/tests are authoritative for the ML boundary.
invariants: A workspace may be execution-feasible without being a durable destination.
A verified copy on disposable, temporary, expiring or otherwise non-durable capacity does not satisfy durable completion.
MLStorageCheckpointValue contains identity/value evidence only; it never exports live journal/controller/foreign handles.
MLDurableFrontierValue carries retained feasible frontier identity and objective scores, not storage ownership.
MLStorageFabricBridge delegates placement and durable-completion decisions to Storage Fabric objects.
ML must not treat successful scratch evaluation as durable experiment completion.
procedure: Export a value-only MLStorageCheckpointValue at the desired historical experiment point.
Export a bounded MLDurableFrontierValue for promoted feasible Pareto points.
Ask StoragePlacementAdvisor for workspace/destination placement under declared capacity and lifecycle.
Use StorageDurableCompletionPolicy to determine whether a safe/stable verified replica exists.
Keep scratch/disposable results provisional until Storage Fabric reports durable completion.

provenance.claim: Authoritative workspace safety, service lifecycle, placement and durable-completion semantics consumed by ML.
Value-only ML checkpoint/frontier exports and delegation bridge to Storage Fabric.
Regression proves disposable verified workspace is not durable completion and safe/stable verified replica is.
